text: I'll start by looking at the workspace layout and finding the pagination code.
The bug is visible at line 31: `end = start + page_size - 1` is an inclusive index, but it's used as an exclusive slice bound, dropping one item per page. Let me read the file to confirm.

Confirmed: `items[start:end]` with `end = start + page_size - 1` returns only `page_size - 1` items per page, so the item at every `page_size`-th position is skipped (with 11 items and size 5, items 5, 10 are lost). I'll fix the slice bound.

args.summary: Fixed an off-by-one in library/pagination.py's paginate(). The slice end was computed as `start + page_size - 1`, which treats the bound as inclusive, but Python slices are exclusive, so each page returned only page_size-1 items and silently dropped the item at every page_size-th position (e.g., items 5 and 10 with 11 items at page size 5). Changed it to `end = start + page_size`. The full test suite passes (29 tests).
